 SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) Shares Up 3.2% - Time to Buy?
 Written by MarketBeat November 17, 2026 Add As Preferred Source Share Share Share This Article Link copied to clipboard. Close 
 Image from MarketBeat Media, LLC. 
 Key Points
 SpaceX shares rose 3.2% to $141.70 in mid-day trading, while trading volume was 16% below its average.
 A first-ever catch of Starship’s upper stage after its return from orbit marked progress toward reusability and potentially lower launch costs. Analysts were broadly positive, with a “Moderate Buy” consensus and an average price target of $243.60.
 SpaceX reported quarterly revenue growth of 161.4% year over year and beat EPS expectations, but a Dec. 8 lock-up expiration could expand the tradable share float by an estimated 17.6%, creating potential selling pressure.
 MarketBeat previews the top five stocks to own by December 1st . 
 SpaceX ( NASDAQ:SPCX - Get Free Report ) rose 3.2% during mid-day trading on Tuesday. The stock traded as high as $142.11 and last traded at $141.70. Approximately 86,764,749 shares changed hands during trading, a decline of 16% from the average session volume of 103,237,938 shares. The stock had previously closed at $137.36. Get SpaceX alerts: Sign Up Key Stories Impacting SpaceX
 Is It Too Late to Buy the Dip? 3 Corners of the Market Still Offering Real Value 
 Investors following SPCX have been watching these stories: Positive Sentiment: SpaceX caught Starship’s upper stage after its return from orbit for the first time, an important step toward reusing the spacecraft and potentially lowering launch costs. The booster was not recovered, but analysts highlighted the upper-stage catch as meaningful progress for Starship and future Starlink deployment. Article 
 Positive Sentiment: Analyst optimism followed the Starship milestone, with reports citing bullish ratings and price targets, including Cantor Fitzgerald’s $345 target. Such forecasts may support sentiment but depend on SpaceX executing its ambitious growth plans. Article 
 Negative Sentiment: A Dec. 8 lock-up expiration could increase SpaceX’s estimated tradable float by about 17.6%, potentially creating near-term selling pressure. Article 
 Wall Street Analysts Forecast Growth
 SPCX has been the subject of a number of analyst reports. Weiss Ratings assumed coverage on SpaceX in a research note on Tuesday, September 1st. They set a "sell (d)" rating for the company. TD Cowen increased their target price on shares of SpaceX from $200.00 to $224.00 and gave the company a "buy" rating in a report on Wednesday, October 21st. Barclays increased their price objective on SpaceX from $254.00 to $300.00 and gave the company an "overweight" rating in a research note on Wednesday, October 21st. KeyCorp reiterated a "sector weight" rating on shares of SpaceX in a report on Friday. Finally, Bank of America raised their target price on shares of SpaceX from $235.00 to $275.00 and gave the company a "buy" rating in a research note on Thursday, October 22nd. Four research analysts have rated the stock with a Strong Buy rating, thirty-one have given a Buy rating, nine have issued a Hold rating and three have assigned a Sell rating to the stock. According to data from MarketBeat.com, the stock presently has an average rating of "Moderate Buy" and a consensus price target of $243.60.
 Golden Dome’s $185 Billion Question: Who Actually Gets Paid? 
 Get Our Latest Analysis on SpaceX SpaceX Stock Performance
 The firm has a market capitalization of $1.92 trillion and a P/E ratio of 545.00. The business has a fifty day moving average of $148.69. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.20, a current ratio of 3.08 and a quick ratio of 3.00. 
 Can NVIDIA Maintain Its Momentum Without Huang? 
 SpaceX ( NASDAQ:SPCX - Get Free Report ) last released its quarterly earnings results on Tuesday, October 20th. The company reported $0.35 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, beating analysts' consensus estimates of $0.10 by $0.25. The company had revenue of $14.57 billion for the quarter. SpaceX had a negative net margin of 8.61% and a negative return on equity of 3.24%. SpaceX's revenue for the quarter was up 161.4% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same period in the previous year, the company earned ($0.36) EPS. As a group, equities analysts predict that SpaceX will post 0.22 EPS for the current year. Insider Buying and Selling at SpaceX
 In other news, COO Gwynne Shotwell sold 342,170 shares of the stock in a transaction that occurred on Tuesday, September 22nd. The shares were sold at an average price of $153.57, for a total transaction of $52,547,046.90. Following the transaction, the chief operating officer directly owned 2,472,035 shares in the company, valued at approximately $379,630,414.95. This trade represents a 12.16% decrease in their ownership of the stock. The transaction was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is accessible through this link . The transaction was executed under a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 trading plan. Institutional Investors Weigh In On SpaceX
 Several institutional investors have recently added to or reduced their stakes in SPCX. SC US Ttgp LTD. acquired a new stake in shares of SpaceX during the 2nd quarter worth approximately $20,933,621,000. Darsana Capital Partners LP purchased a new position in SpaceX in the 2nd quarter valued at $17,335,783,000. K5 Global Advisor LLC purchased a new stake in SpaceX during the 2nd quarter valued at about $6,587,531,000. Mirae Asset Global Investments Co. Ltd. purchased a new position in SpaceX during the third quarter worth approximately $4,224,143,000. Finally, Thrive Capital Management LLC acquired a new stake in SpaceX during the second quarter worth about $3,231,681,000. SpaceX Company Profile
 ( Get Free Report ) Space Exploration Technologies Corp., commonly known as SpaceX, is a privately held aerospace company founded in 2002 by Elon Musk. The company develops and operates launch vehicles and spacecraft designed to reduce the cost of access to space and support commercial, government and scientific missions. SpaceX’s principal products and services include the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets, the Dragon spacecraft and the Starlink satellite communications network. Falcon rockets are used to launch satellites, cargo and crew, while Dragon spacecraft support transportation to and from low Earth orbit. Featured Articles
